_comment: 🔮️ Test-only references of the pets product (Protocol v2). Every case under ../🧪️tests names one of these oracles or the recorded no-oracle decision; the TypeScript twin (@semio-tech/pets) and the Rust twin (semio-framework-pets) are the subjects and are additionally held to each other. The Python references live inside the case adapters (🧪️tests/*/🐍️.py) and use numpy, scipy and jsonschema only. Shared vectors under ../🧫️fixtures are generated from those same adapters by the ticket scripts named in every feature, so a committed vector and its oracle can never disagree.

engine.implementation: numpy.sin, numpy.cos, numpy.arctan2 and numpy.exp, numpy.random.SeedSequence.generate_state, numpy.linalg (inv, norm, matrix_power), numpy.interp, numpy.hypot, numpy.cross, numpy.cumsum and numpy.searchsorted

oracles.rationale: The pets core is a deterministic fold restricted to exact arithmetic, square roots and 32-bit integer operations (design §2.4), so each of its numeric modules has a closed mathematical reading numpy evaluates independently: sine and cosine of 2π·t for the polynomial `sinTurns`/`cosTurns` (case 📐️turn-trigonometry, tolerance 1e-9 around an owned error bound of 1e-12), and in the same case `numpy.arctan2` and `numpy.exp` for the polynomial arctangent `atanTurns` and the rational decay `fastNegExp`, each judged within its stated error (2e-6 turns; 1.9e-2, and 6e-4 up to 1) and projected as the restated double with its bit pattern; `numpy.random.SeedSequence(key).generate_state(count)` for the counter-based draws, whose words must match bit for bit (case 🎲️counter-randomness); 3×3 homogeneous matrix products and `numpy.linalg.inv` for the forward kinematics and inverses of the rig (case 🦴️rig-solving); `numpy.linalg.norm` for the look offset and `numpy.linalg.matrix_power` of the semi-implicit Euler step matrix for the gaze and settling springs (cases 👀️gaze-tracking, 🪀️spring-settling); membership on a sampled grid and closed forms for perches and strides (case 🏞️terrain-walking); `numpy.hypot` for the length of a ladder and the place of its climber, the lean as a ratio and the rungs as the whole spacings that fit, `numpy.cumsum` of the eased speeds for the climb, and the separating axes of a segment and a box — extents and the signs of `numpy.cross` products, laid over 4097 sampled points of the segment — for the clear line of a ladder, which the core clips by Liang–Barsky (case 🪜️ladder-geometry); `numpy.cumsum` with `numpy.searchsorted` for weighted picks and the drift arithmetic of rapport (cases 🧠️behavior-choice, 🤝️bond-dynamics); `uint32` array arithmetic, which wraps at 32 bits by itself, for the particle hash `lowbias32`/`mix` and its five published words, a pool simulation walked tick by tick for the births and lives the stateless `particlesOf` derives from a window of indices, `numpy.sin`, `numpy.cos` and `numpy.clip` for the five motions with the rational decay held to `numpy.exp` within 0.02, and a stable `numpy.argsort` for the cap (case ✨️particle-motion); Python's `str.startswith` at a `/` for the topic match, `numpy.floor` and `numpy.clip` for the pick, permutations of `numpy.random.Generator` for the property that a pick never follows a value, a correctness flag or an answer, one vectorised boolean expression for the gates, `numpy.argmax` for the station with the most room and a branch-free path of `numpy.interp` ramps and `numpy.sin` for the lifted copy (case 🪄️mischief-choice). The moods of case 💗️feeling-dynamics are piecewise linear in time: numpy evaluates the trajectory of a feeling over a whole array of ticks as one closed form (`numpy.maximum`, `numpy.minimum`, `numpy.where`), finds the tick a mood has faded and the tick a feeling settles as the first sample by `numpy.argmax` instead of solving for them, holds the steps between consecutive ticks to the rates with `numpy.diff`, proves the ranks a strict order in the tiers of the design with a boolean matrix product and `numpy.argsort`, vectorises a crowd over everybody who catches a mood while asserting beat by beat that no intensity leaves [0, 1] and nobody ends above the strongest of its mood, and reads faces and weights off `numpy.interp`. Surveyed and declined: gl-matrix, d3-ease and polygon-clipping are JavaScript libraries and can judge the TypeScript twin inside its unit suites only, never the Rust twin; pure-rand and seedrandom implement other generator families than the SeedSequence hash-mix; mathjs has no SeedSequence and no bit-exact 32-bit stream.

packages.role: Array arithmetic, `numpy.interp` between keys and the sampled grids the scipy routines are evaluated on.

engine.implementation: scipy.optimize.brentq, scipy.integrate.solve_ivp, scipy.interpolate.CubicHermiteSpline, scipy.linalg.expm, scipy.optimize.isotonic_regression, scipy.optimize.minimize (SLSQP), scipy.signal.find_peaks and scipy.sparse.csgraph

oracles.rationale: Three parts of the core solve something a general numeric library solves differently: the cubic Bézier easing inverts x(s) by 48 bisection steps, which `scipy.optimize.brentq` on the same polynomial reproduces within 1e-9 (case 🎞️animation-sampling, with `numpy.interp` for the linear stretches between keys); the hop between perches is a ballistic arc integrated tick by tick, which `scipy.integrate.solve_ivp` and the roots of the arc bound (case 🦘️hop-ballistics); and every activity must stay reachable from every other through the weights of the behaviour table, which `scipy.sparse.csgraph` decides on the transition graph (case 🧠️behavior-choice). Case ⚗️chemistry-rules adds a fourth: whether every state of a species can be reached from its resting state — by its tricks, by states that last and give way, by the reactions of the menagerie — is `scipy.sparse.csgraph.breadth_first_order` on the graph of its states, and a state nothing leads to fails the oracle; beside it numpy reads the state at a tick off the unrolled chain of states (`numpy.cumsum`, `numpy.searchsorted`) where the cores take whole laps off a circle, picks a trick by `numpy.searchsorted` in the running weights, and matches reactions for all ordered pairs of actors at once — bodies as boxes, gaps and overlaps as broadcast matrices, traits as masks, the due reactions listed in pair order by `numpy.argwhere`. Cases 🪢️swing-dynamics and 🪂️parachute-descent add what hangs and what descends: the one constrained Verlet step (SHAKE) of a held pet, a pet under a canopy and a pet on a reeled rope approximates a pendulum, and `scipy.integrate.solve_ivp` (DOP853, tolerances 1e-12) integrates that pendulum itself — with a fixed or an accelerated pivot, a prescribed shortening length and the drag a damping factor stands for — so every committed swing must stay within the degrees it states (0.4° over three seconds for ropes and canopies) and keep its amplitude within 0.05° over a minute, while the usual shortcut that pulls the point back onto the circle, run from the same start as a negative control, must lose more than 10° or the oracle refuses to answer; `scipy.linalg.expm` advances the continuous spring the follow spring discretises, `numpy.polyfit(deg=2)` yields the slope the seven integer weights of the release velocity must reproduce (`fractions.Fraction` shows the weights exact), `numpy.arctan2` judges cone and lean, and the descent under a canopy is held to the closed form of its first-order lag (`numpy.exp`, `numpy.cumsum`) and to `solve_ivp` with events for whole drops. Both cases project the oracle's own restatement of the step once the libraries have confirmed it within the stated physical tolerance, because that tolerance is far coarser than the comparison's 1e-9. Cases 🧗️wall-climbing and 🎣️grapple-reach add how pets get up: the mantle over a rim is three eased parts between the keys of its definition, which `scipy.interpolate.CubicHermiteSpline` with flat ends reproduces within 1e-9, and the haul on a slanted rope is the reeled pendulum of case 🪢️swing-dynamics begun at rest half a tick before its first step, which `solve_ivp` follows within 0.4° while the rope is longer than 0.4 of its start; beside them numpy cuts the free stretches of the surveyed walls by membership on a quarter-pixel grid (`numpy.diff` of boolean masks, no interval is subtracted), judges every line of sight by the separating axes of segment and box (`numpy.cross`) laid over 4097 sampled points instead of clipping it, picks the hook point by `numpy.argmin`, and holds climbs, slides, zips and hook flights to their closed forms (`numpy.cumsum`, `numpy.minimum`, `numpy.hypot`). Case 🚧️clearance-proof adds how pets keep apart: the seating of a perch group after a survey is a quadratic programme (the least squares of the moves, subject to the order, a seam between neighbours and the ends of the perch), which `scipy.optimize.isotonic_regression`, clipped into the perch, solves within 1e-9 of the pooled seats the cores compute and `scipy.optimize.minimize` (SLSQP) on the programme itself within 1e-5; beside them numpy judges every overlap by the area two boxes share (broadcast `minimum` and `maximum`, pairs by `numpy.argwhere`), finds free places and guarded strides by searching the 1/64 px lattice instead of carving intervals (`numpy.argmin`, `numpy.argmax`), samples every claim densely — slices as `numpy.minimum.reduceat` and `numpy.maximum.reduceat` hulls of the path, every owner a time line of one box per tick — so that a plan is clear when no two time lines share an area at one tick, finds heads by boolean masks over all tops, and holds every push of a held body to a place that shares nothing with any obstacle. Case 👆️gesture-recognition adds the learner's hand, which the cores recognise tick by tick with comparisons only and the reference reads whole: `numpy.unwrap` of `numpy.arctan2` is the winding of the pointer round a pet, so every committed circle must end a full turn in its direction and every circle the reading finds clean must be cued; `scipy.signal.find_peaks` with a prominence finds the reversals of a petting in the horizontal offset and of a shake along twelve directions and the principal axis (`numpy.linalg.eigh`), so every committed petting and shake must follow the reversals that make it and every clean one must be cued; ordinary pointer travel and carrying must set off nothing and hide no clean gesture; and the press and the heat are read in closed form — `numpy.hypot` and `numpy.flatnonzero` for what a press becomes, Lindley's recursion as `numpy.cumsum` minus its `numpy.minimum.accumulate` and `numpy.searchsorted` for the tiers of attention. Surveyed and declined: d3-ease has no general cubic-bezier (its eases are fixed families; it judges the TypeScript twin's `smoothstep` only), bezier-easing is not in the lockfile, CSS engines cannot be reached from the harness, and shapely and scikit-learn (boxes, `IsotonicRegression`) are not in the harness environment.

The contract 🧬️schema/🔣️.json is JSON Schema draft-07 and normative; the product validates menageries, species and ensembles with its own validator (menagerieIssues, speciesIssues, ensembleIssues) and links no schema library at runtime. python-jsonschema's Draft7Validator reads the normative file itself and judges every committed document of case 🧬️schema-conformance: the sample menagerie, each of its species and its ensemble must conform; every structurally broken document must break the schema at the keyword and pointer its vector names; and every document that breaks a rule of design §3 is judged for what the schema can say about it — it either conforms (the rule lies beyond JSON Schema: duplicate ids, unresolved references, bone order, key order, loop seams, gait clips, hover, duplicate bonds and scenes) or breaks the named keyword (ranges, colours, ease abscissas, the two different species of a bond, the core of a cast). The codes and pointers of those rule findings are recomputed beside it in the adapter by a second implementation written from the design text — a supplement that holds the two cores to one reading of the rules, not third-party evidence. ajv (pets-ajv-structure) judges the same contract inside the TypeScript unit suite — two independent schema engines.

Judges the owned validator inside the unit suite `🔨️modules/✅️validation/🧪️tests/🔬️unit` of @semio-tech/pets (vitest, devDependency of the core package): ajv compiles the normative 🧬️schema/🔣️.json and, for every tested menagerie, species and ensemble, accepts the document exactly when the owned validator reports no finding the schema can express, and rejects every structurally broken document at the pointer the owned validator names. It is the JavaScript engine beside python-jsonschema (pets-jsonschema), which judges the same contract in the Protocol v2 case.

engine.implementation: mat2d (multiply, invert, translate, rotate, scale, fromRotation) and vec2.transformMat2d

oracles.rationale: Judges the owned affine arithmetic and the owned sine and cosine inside the unit suites `🔨️modules/🦴️rig/🧪️tests/🔬️unit` and `🔨️modules/📐️trigonometry/🧪️tests/🔬️unit` of @semio-tech/pets (vitest, devDependency of the core package). gl-matrix's mat2d has the layout of the rig's `Affine`: `compose` must equal `mat2d.multiply(parent, local)` and `transform` must equal `vec2.transformMat2d` bit for bit, `invert` must agree with `mat2d.invert` within 1e-11 and answer the identity exactly where gl-matrix refuses to invert, and every solved skeleton must agree with the chain gl-matrix translates, rotates, scales and multiplies bone by bone. `sinTurns` and `cosTurns` are held to `mat2d.fromRotation` on 65 537 angles over ±8 turns within the module's error bound of 1e-12. It is the JavaScript engine beside numpy (pets-numpy), which judges the same modules in the Protocol v2 cases 🦴️rig-solving and 📐️turn-trigonometry; the React target registers the same library for its drawing rules (pets-react-gl-matrix).

engine.implementation: d3-ease easeLinear, easeQuadIn, easeQuadOut, easeCubicIn, easeCubicOut and easeCubicInOut

oracles.rationale: Judges the owned easing inside the unit suite `🔨️modules/🎞️animation/🧪️tests/🔬️unit` of @semio-tech/pets (vitest, devDependency of the core package). A polynomial ease is a cubic Bézier whose abscissa is linear (control points at one and two thirds), so `easeBezier` with those control points must reproduce d3-ease's `easeLinear`, `easeQuadIn`, `easeQuadOut`, `easeCubicIn` and `easeCubicOut` within 1e-13 on 1025 amounts; the CSS ease-in-out, which no d3 ease equals, is held to the family of `easeCubicInOut` (symmetric, rising, on the same side of the diagonal, never 0.1 apart). d3-ease has no general cubic-bezier: the bisection itself is judged by `scipy.optimize.brentq` (pets-scipy) in the Protocol v2 case 🎞️animation-sampling.

Judges the owned interval arithmetic of the perches inside the unit suite `🔨️modules/🏞️terrain/🧪️tests/🔬️unit` of @semio-tech/pets (vitest, devDependency of the core package). `perchesOf` cuts the free stretches of a surface with plain comparisons; polygon-clipping reaches the same stretches as geometry: the strip of the surface intersected with the viewport, minus the column of every keep-out whose box overlaps the headroom band above the strip with an area. On 300 generated layouts of surfaces and keep-outs the two must name the same perches. It is the JavaScript engine beside numpy (pets-numpy), which judges the perches by membership on a sampled grid in the Protocol v2 case 🏞️terrain-walking. The same suite turns the method by a quarter for `wallsOf`: the wall as a strip intersected with the viewport, minus the row of every keep-out whose box overlaps the band on its air side, from the lip to the clearance, must name the same pitches on 300 generated layouts; numpy judges them on a grid in case 🧗️wall-climbing.

engine.implementation: mat2d (translate, rotate, scale, multiply, fromValues, fromTranslation, fromRotation, fromScaling, determinant) and vec2 (transformMat2d, distance, lerp, normalize, dot, cross)

oracles.rationale: Judges the owned SVG depiction of @semio-tech/pets-react inside its suite `🧪️tests/🖌️pet-depiction` (vitest in jsdom, devDependency of the react package). gl-matrix's mat2d has the layout of an SVG `matrix(a b c d e f)`; it composes the rig of the tested species bone by bone (translate, rotate, scale, then the parent's matrix), and every `transform` the depiction writes must parse back to those six numbers within the three decimals the drawing rules round to (design §6.2). It also carries points through what was written: the tip of a limb through the matrix of its group, and a pupil through bone, eye offset and lid squash, which must land where gl-matrix puts them. The frames the depiction is given are gl-matrix's own, so the suite does not lean on the core's rig solver, which numpy judges in case 🦴️rig-solving. The same library judges the drawings of the second round. In `🧪️tests/🧰️gear-depiction` gl-matrix composes the placement of a tilted actor the way the stage means it — its feet, a turn on screen about the pivot, then the mirror and the size — and the CSS transform the gear writes (a mirrored drawing turned the other way round inside its box) must carry every point to the same place; the groups of the tools must undo mirror and tilt, so that drawing and group together are a plain translation and scaling; the parachute must hang from where gl-matrix carries the scruff, its cords must end where gl-matrix carries the rim of the canopy, the gun must sit in the carried hand with its muzzle where a rotation by the aim puts it, the hook must point along the normalised arrival of the rope, and the rails and rungs of carried and standing ladders, carried through the written matrices, must be perpendicular (dot product), evenly spaced and of the stated length. In `🧪️tests/🎆️effect-painting` every particle's `transform` must equal the placement gl-matrix composes from its place, turn and size under the root's scaling, and every blob of a puff of dust (an outline circle in ink under a fill circle in paper, both of one middle and radius) must lie where gl-matrix carries its middle and its rim: the middle of the vanished body risen by the phase, then for a blob of the ring a turn by its angle carried onto the ellipse of the body's half-width and half-height, spread by the phase, all under the root's scaling. The no-write, pooling and tint claims of both suites are held to jsdom's `MutationObserver` records and call spies, not to a library. In `🧪️tests/🪞️fixture-lifting` the copy of a lifted host element must lie where gl-matrix carries the corners of the original's box: moved by the lift in the pets' pixels times their size, then turned by the lift's tilt about its middle (the CSS `transform-origin: 50% 50%` composed as translate, rotate, translate back).

engine.implementation: aria-query `roles` map: the WAI-ARIA 1.2 role model with each role's superclasses, queried directly and through @testing-library/dom's `getRoles`, `queryAllByRole` and `isInaccessible`

oracles.rationale: Judges three claims of @semio-tech/pets-react inside its suites (vitest in jsdom, devDependency of the react package). In `🧪️tests/🪞️fixture-lifting` the copy of a lifted host element must be decoration like the pets: @testing-library/dom's accessibility tree must hold none of its nodes (`getRoles` empty, `isInaccessible` true for every node), whatever controls, links, labels and roles the original holds. In `🧪️tests/🫥️decorative-layer` the pet layer must be decoration (design §6.5): with a cast on stage, @testing-library/dom's accessibility tree — built on aria-query's role model — must hold no node of the layer (`getRoles` is empty for it, `isInaccessible` is true for the layer and every descendant) and a query for each of aria-query's concrete roles must find nothing in it. In `🧪️tests/📡️surface-survey` the default keep-outs must cover what a person can operate (design §6.3): every role the selector of controls names must be a concrete widget role by aria-query's superclass chains, and over a sample of native and ARIA elements the selector must match exactly those whose role — implicit by @testing-library/dom, or explicit — aria-query calls a widget. The geometry of the survey is held to shared vectors (`🧫️fixtures/📡️surface-survey`) computed by a second reading of the design written in Python from the design text (`generate_survey_vectors.py` of ticket 2026/10/02/QUIZ-PETS: tag and attribute tables instead of a selector engine, interval arithmetic) — a supplement, never third-party evidence; no library measures a page into surfaces and keep-outs by these rules. Frame pacing (`🧪️tests/⏲️frame-pacing`) runs on a hand-driven clock and on the fake clock of vitest itself.

engine.implementation: userEvent.setup().pointer (mouse, touch and multi-touch presses, moves and releases with coordinates and text offsets) and .keyboard (Escape, Enter, Shift, typing), dispatching the browser's sequences of pointer, mouse, focus, selection and click events

oracles.rationale: Judges the learner's hand of @semio-tech/pets-react (`🔨️modules/🤏️grasp`, design-v2 §14.1, §17, §22) inside its suite `🧪️tests/🤏️pet-handling` (vitest in jsdom, devDependency of the react package). user-event plays the browser's side of a press as the Pointer Events and UI Events specifications describe it: a cancelled `pointerdown` suppresses the compatible `mousedown` and with it focus and the start of a text selection, but not the click, which goes to the nearest common ancestor of where the press began and ended; a press that is not cancelled focuses what it lands on and selects text as it moves; a label hands its click on to its control. Held against that model: a press on a pet with nothing interactive beneath it reaches no listener of the page (no `pointerdown`, `mousedown` or `click` on the element beneath or the document, no focus, no selection), while the same press beside the pet reaches all of them; a press on a button, a label or a host's grip under a pet is the control's (it is clicked, focused, checked); words beside the pets are selected by a drag and a selection holds the next press back from the pets; Escape calls a held pet off and is kept from the page, every other Escape and the keyboard's click pass; a tap with a finger is a press like a mouse's and its click is swallowed; a second finger is never a press of its own. The stage events the layer hands the core (pressed, the latest drag of a frame, released, cancelled, played, permitted, stirred, scrolled) are held by a fake core in the same suite; the walls of the survey by the shared vectors of `🧫️fixtures/📡️surface-survey` (see pets-react-aria-query).

noOracleDecisions.rationale: The stage (design §5) is this product's own simulation: events folded into actors that idle, walk, hop, fall, glance, blink and meet each other on surveyed perches. No third-party library simulates this model, and a second engine written to be compared with it would be this model again. Case 🎪️stage-trace therefore rests on scripted event logs committed as specification vectors — the projection is a digest of every frame's numbers — and on laws that hold for every log: actors stand on perches, never inside keep-outs, at most the mode's number of movers, at most one encounter, the same seed and events yield the same frames. Every building block the stage calls (trigonometry, randomness, rig, animation, terrain, behaviour) has a third-party oracle of its own. The TypeScript core and its Rust twin each replay every log, and the harness compares their projections digest for digest at every checkpoint: two separately compiled cores that agree on the IEEE-754 bit patterns of every frame are the `independent-implementations` substitute.

comparisonProfiles.description: Structural identity with the pets numeric parity tolerance of 1e-9 (design §10), applied as an absolute difference; projections compared under it are scaled so that 1e-9 is also their relative bound. Ids, kinds, orders, integers and every non-numeric field still compare exactly.

subjectFeatures.rationale: 🧪️ The pets crate re-exports its JSON codec (serde_json with `float_roundtrip`, so every committed decimal becomes the double JSON.parse and Python read) only under `sut`: the Rust subject adapters decode the shared vectors into the typed twins and encode their answers with it, while production builds of the crate stay free of serde_json.

oracleHostPackages.rationale: 📐️ Sine and cosine, SeedSequence words, homogeneous matrices, norms, matrix powers and cumulative weights of the numeric references.
🎞️ Root finding on the Bézier easing, integration of the hop arc, of the pendulum behind every swing and of the descent under a canopy, and reachability of the behaviour graph.
🧬️ Draft 7 validation of every pets document against the normative schema.
